questions.description: How does energy availability or restriction affect exercise adaptation and performance?
questions.gap: Dual-experienced strength-running populations, long-term outcomes and safe individualized targets remain unresolved.

questions.description: How does an energy surplus affect resistance-training adaptation?
questions.gap: No optimal surplus or combined running outcome established.

questions.description: How does acute carbohydrate ingestion affect resistance exercise?
questions.gap: Long-term effects, isoenergetic controls and hybrid dose response remain uncertain.

questions.description: How does carbohydrate ingestion affect short-term glycogen restoration?
questions.gap: Subsequent session and long-term outcomes in hybrid athletes remain unresolved.

questions.description: Does periodic carbohydrate restriction improve endurance adaptation?
questions.gap: No validated hybrid nutritional periodization or individualized restriction rule.

questions.description: How does protein supplementation influence concurrent exercise adaptation?
questions.gap: No direct requirement or adequately fueled dual-experienced running dose-response established.

questions.description: How does protein intake affect adaptation to resistance training?
questions.gap: Indirect transfer to endurance/concurrent training; energy-restriction context differs.

questions.description: What metabolic evidence informs protein requirements during endurance training?
questions.gap: No definitive long-term performance dose or concurrent-training requirement.

questions.description: How reliable are food and wearable energy observations?
questions.gap: Individual estimates, deduplication and calibration require Packet 007.

questions.description: How should nutrition inform coordinated training decisions?
questions.gap: No reviewed adaptive intervention policy or clinical screening algorithm.

claims.assertion: Ten days of lower energy availability reduced integrated myofibrillar protein synthesis relative to the adequate-EA condition in trained women performing combined exercise.
claims.limitations: Thirty participants; short metabolic endpoint, diet components vary; not long-term strength/hypertrophy or diagnosis.
claims.assessment: Randomized controlled feeding and standardized exercise support study-specific effect; dual-experienced runner and male transfer not reviewed.

support.locator: Results: Daily integrated myofibrillar and sarcoplasmic muscle protein synthesis; Fig. 3A.
support.result: Change −0.08 percentage points/day (95% CI −0.13 to −0.03) in LEA vs +0.10 (0.05 to 0.14) in OEA; group-by-time p<0.0001.
support.restriction: Study provided 2.2 g protein/kg lean mass/day in both groups; assigned EA 25 vs 50 kcal/kg FFM/day.

claims.assertion: The low-EA dietary period impaired 20-minute cycling time-trial power relative to the adequate-EA period.
claims.limitations: Short crossover intervention; carryover and dietary covariation need review. Cycling not running; performance already reported elsewhere.
claims.assessment: Controlled crossover and CI support narrow finding; running and long-term transfer unapproved.

support.restriction: Twelve women; within-LEA −16.8 W; achieved EA 22.3 vs 51.9 kcal/kg FFM/day.

claims.assertion: Parallel comparisons in the review favored resistance training without energy deficiency for lean-mass gains.
claims.limitations: Small number of studies; mixed population, variable energy deficits and lean mass measurement. Full-text result verification outstanding.
claims.assessment: Direction supported by abstract and body excerpts; CI and population details require independent full-text check.

support.locator: Abstract Results, Analysis A; body text Fig. 2A rounding requires verification.
support.result: ES −0.57, p=.02 (abstract; body text −0.58). CI not reliably extracted.
support.restriction: Analysis A only; seven studies for lean mass.

claims.assertion: The parallel strength comparisons did not establish a clear difference between resistance training with and without energy deficit.
claims.limitations: Limited precision and population directness; cannot infer no impairment for an experienced hybrid athlete.
claims.assessment: Abstract and accessible excerpt; verify interval and methods before use.

support.locator: Abstract Results, Analysis A; body text Fig. 2B.
support.result: ES −0.31, p=.28; CI not reliably extracted.
support.restriction: Five strength studies; no equivalence test.

claims.assertion: Across participants, change in body mass was positively associated with change in skinfold thickness.
claims.limitations: Small underpowered sample, skinfold proxy, no running outcome; bench 1RM group result differs.
claims.assessment: Association only; does not establish optimal surplus or causal dose response.

support.locator: Results regression analysis; abstract Results (BF and R²).
support.restriction: Secondary regression across 17 completers; not randomized dose-effect estimate.

claims.assertion: Acute carbohydrate ingestion increased completed resistance exercise volume in pooled crossover comparisons.
claims.limitations: High heterogeneity; imputed correlations; no chronic strength or optimal dose; low GRADE.
claims.assessment: Full-text estimate, but variable protocols and risk of bias; transfer conditional on demand and prior intake.

support.locator: Results §3.4 Fig. 3 and Table 4, overall volume estimate.
support.restriction: Acute volume only; comparator often noncaloric.

claims.assertion: Postexercise carbohydrate increased short-term muscle glycogen restoration rate compared with water.
claims.limitations: Biochemical endpoint; variable exercise protocols and energy difference; no next-session performance estimate.
claims.assessment: Pooled result direction consistent in sensitivity analyses; indirect for programming a double day.

support.restriction: 10 trials, 86 participants; mean CHO 1.02 g/kg body mass/h.

claims.assertion: Adding protein to carbohydrate did not demonstrate a faster glycogen restoration rate in the studied short-recovery comparisons.
claims.limitations: No equivalence test; distinct protein-related remodeling outcomes not addressed.
claims.assessment: Direct biochemical comparison but not a general conclusion about recovery or protein.

support.locator: Results Part 2, pooled CHO+PRO versus CHO.
support.restriction: 19 trials, 160 participants; carbohydrate amounts not identical across all comparisons.

claims.assertion: The pooled performance estimate did not establish superiority of periodized carbohydrate restriction over normal/high availability.
claims.limitations: Small sample of heterogeneous protocols and sports; energy matching varies; no equivalence.
claims.assessment: Interval includes small unfavorable and favorable effects; no approved hybrid transfer.

support.restriction: Nine studies; not a comparison of every possible carbohydrate timing policy.

claims.assertion: Five of nine longer-term studies assessing muscle mass reported enhanced gains with protein supplementation during concurrent training.
claims.limitations: Abstract-only; dietary control, trial overlap, outcome definitions and study-level effects require review.
claims.assessment: Direct exercise combination but largely untrained and no dose-response synthesis. Keep pending, not operational.

support.locator: Abstract Results, longer-term studies, muscle mass.
support.result: 5/9 studies; no pooled estimate or CI.
support.restriction: Review-level study count, not an effect size; total longer-term sample 167 trained and 391 untrained across ten studies.

claims.assertion: None of the six included aerobic-capacity studies reported an additional VO2max/peak gain from protein supplementation.
claims.limitations: Abstract-only, heterogeneous diets and training, uncertain power.
claims.assessment: No direct hybrid requirement inference; full-text appraisal outstanding.

support.result: 0/6 reported additional benefit; no pooled estimate or CI.
support.restriction: Study count; not evidence of equivalence or other endurance outcomes.

claims.assertion: Protein supplementation modestly increased pooled fat-free-mass gains during resistance training.
claims.limitations: Mixed training history, baseline diets and comparators; FFM includes water; not direct hybrid evidence.
claims.assessment: Pooled controlled interventions; inspect subgroup and trial bias before transfer.

support.restriction: 49 studies overall; outcome-specific count not extracted here.

claims.assertion: Protein supplementation modestly increased pooled 1RM gains during resistance training.
claims.limitations: Not lift-specific prediction or individualized requirement; populations and controls differ.
claims.assessment: Indirect for dual-experienced athletes; review precision and comparator.

support.restriction: Pooled absolute kg across different strength tests.

claims.assertion: The study-arm segmented regression estimated a plateau in FFM gains at a total protein intake near 1.62 g/kg body mass/day.
claims.limitations: Wide CI, confounding, no concurrent or deficit-specific estimate.
claims.assessment: Modeled association; no approved use as a nutritional cutoff.

support.restriction: 42 arms, 723 participants; arm-level estimate, not individual threshold.

claims.assertion: A graded-protein metabolic study estimated a protein requirement of 1.65 g/kg body mass/day on a high-volume endurance-training day.
claims.limitations: Metabolic estimator, not measured long-term strength/endurance performance; no combined program.
claims.assessment: Useful complementary evidence; method and directness limit precise coaching prescription.

support.locator: Abstract Results and Discussion, labeled CO2 excretion breakpoint.
support.result: 1.65 g/kg/day; upper 95% confidence bound 1.83; alternative oxidation endpoint 1.53, upper bound 1.70.
support.restriction: Simulated 35 km over three days, 20 km run test day, adequate/high carbohydrate.

claims.assertion: Self-reported energy intake was lower on average than doubly labeled water energy expenditure in the reviewed athlete studies.
claims.limitations: Actual energy balance may differ, reporting methods heterogeneous; no individual correction factor.
claims.assessment: Measurement warning, not a physiological intervention or TEE estimate.

support.result: Mean reported underestimation 19%; pooled ES −1.006 (95% CI −1.3 to −0.7).
support.restriction: Comparison of intake with expenditure, not direct measurement of intake error alone.

claims.assertion: The systematic review did not identify a commercial wearable brand with accurate energy-expenditure estimates under its evaluated criteria.
claims.limitations: Brand and protocol specific, algorithms change; no current device or individual error estimate.
claims.assessment: Abstract-only extraction; check EE-specific denominators, criteria and recent studies before approval.

support.result: No pooled quantitative EE estimate extracted.
support.restriction: 158 publications across all reviewed outcomes, nine brands; search through May 2019.

methods.question: nutrition-integrated-planning
methods.description: Review training and fueling with actions constrained by per-variable coverage; distinguish absent, partial and reported values.
methods.provenance: Original candidate methodology, Fitness Intelligence Research Packet 004, §§3–4; related empirical records are pending.
methods.tradeoffs: Conservative engineering and methodology; no inferred intake, EA or diagnosis. More logging is optional and not always appropriate.

methods.question: nutrition-integrated-planning
methods.description: Plan feasible carbohydrate and protein opportunities around priority sessions, especially demanding doubles.
methods.provenance: Original candidate methodology, Fitness Intelligence Research Packet 004, §§3–4; related empirical records are pending.
methods.tradeoffs: Acute outcomes do not establish chronic benefit; schedule changes may be preferable to impractical fueling. No mandatory spacing or dose.

methods.question: nutrition-integrated-planning
methods.description: Review plausible energy and fueling constraints before escalating combined workload or pursuing a body-composition goal.
methods.provenance: Original candidate methodology, Fitness Intelligence Research Packet 004, §§3–4; related empirical records are pending.
methods.tradeoffs: Policy has no validated trigger or comparative efficacy; clinical concerns require referral, not automated REDs scoring.

methods.question: nutrition-integrated-planning
methods.description: Discuss feasible total energy, protein, dietary fat and carbohydrate availability across the session/day/block horizons.
methods.provenance: Original candidate methodology, Fitness Intelligence Research Packet 004, §§3–4; related empirical records are pending.
methods.tradeoffs: Ranges are contextual and not independently optimized or summed; no numeric defaults or individualized diet prescription.
